observation.visible_scene: A chocolate-coated ice cream bar stands tilted upright on a white tray, its lower end gripped by a copper binder clip. The bar's coating is broken on the lower right, exposing a pale interior, and a small pool of cream-colored melted liquid sits on the tray beneath the clip. The background is a bright white dotted surface, with a small owl logo watermark in the bottom-right corner. The framing and background stay fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The pale melted puddle at the base slowly spreads and grows slightly larger over the ~2.7-second segment, extending a little to the right and left of the clip.
The thin white drip running down from the broken right edge of the coating appears to lengthen marginally as the clip progresses.
The ice cream bar, its tilt, and the copper clip remain stationary; no translation or rotation of the bar is observed.
The camera viewpoint and background do not shift, so the visible changes are object-side (melting), not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: When melting began and how much liquid had already pooled before the first frame.
The final extent of melting or whether the bar tips over after the last frame.
Why the bar is held by a binder clip and the source video's full context.
uncertain_details: The exact melt rate and whether the drip lengthening is real or a lighting/reflection difference.
Any sub-pixel camera drift is not clearly distinguishable from a perfectly static shot.
